bigPicture.note: These are YouTubers' claims, not advice.

agree.title: Where they agree
agree.text: Post-midterm years have been strong for stocks. Their cited stat: about 16% for the S&P over the next 12 months.

views.title: The index fund itself is the risk
Power, crypto and Tesla
views.detail: AI power as the last growth engine.

views.title: Follow government spending
views.detail: Plus a cash cushion and a dollar hedge.

videos.title: The Government is DESPERATE for You to Start This Business
videos.gist: The government already pays small businesses million-dollar contracts for ordinary work. He says the winners research early on SAM.gov and USAspending.gov. They don't wait for an RFP and fire off proposals.

points.title: Five real small-business awards
points.text: Tree maintenance ($1.76M), fire alarm upgrades ($690K, about $510M a year in spend), kosher/halal food for federal prisons ($1M), hospital wandering-protection alarms (about $150M a year), and an $18M airplane hangar repair.

points.title: Don't chase RFPs
points.text: Writing proposals on SAM.gov is the last step. He says companies that only do that rarely win.

points.title: Research past awards first
points.text: On USAspending.gov, look up your NAICS or keywords. See yearly spend, which agencies buy, which states get the work, and who already wins.

points.title: Answer Sources Sought early
points.text: These are questions, not bids. Send your capability statement and recommendations before the solicitation comes out. If you can't do the whole job, look for a teammate or a subcontract.

points.title: Check procurement forecasts
points.text: Acquisition.gov and the Navy long-range forecast list upcoming work, dollar ranges, incumbents, a contracting contact, and the target quarter. Funding can still change.

points.title: For Penguin Air
points.text: You don't have to learn all of government contracting. Just how the government buys HVAC and plumbing. Start with facilities and mechanical work near bases and federal buildings in the Carolinas.

todo: Search USAspending.gov for HVAC, plumbing and facilities maintenance spend near NC
On SAM.gov, filter Sources Sought for mechanical, HVAC and plumbing work
Note bonding, licenses, past performance and base-access requirements before you reply
Check Acquisition.gov forecasts (and nearby DoD ones) for upcoming facilities jobs
If a Sources Sought is bigger than you can do alone, find a teammate or offer to subcontract
videos.watch: This is also a pitch for his paid GovClose program. The dollar figures are his read of public data and they change. No contract is guaranteed.

videos.title: Build Your Own AI Chief of Staff in 6 Steps
videos.gist: You don't need your own AI model. Connect the right pieces and you get an assistant that knows your business and does tasks for you.

points.title: 1. Give it a home
points.text: A computer or cloud server that runs 24/7. He prefers the cloud.

points.title: 2. Install an agentic harness
points.text: Tools so it can click, type and run tasks. He uses Hermes.

points.title: 3. Choose its AI brain
points.text: Claude, ChatGPT or an open-source model.

points.title: 4. Teach it who you are
points.text: Let it interview you about your business, offers, clients and goals.

points.title: 5. Give it a persistent memory
points.text: A second brain tied to your files, contacts and key info.

points.title: 6. Add skills
points.text: Explain a job once. It remembers and repeats it every day.

todo: Pick a home that runs 24/7 (a cloud server is easiest)
Install an agent harness that can click, type and run tasks
Choose the AI model that powers it
Let it interview you about your business, offers, clients and goals
Connect its memory to your files, contacts and key info
Teach it one job at a time as a saved skill
videos.watch: Lead-magnet reel: 'comment JARVIS' gets you his guide. 'One weekend' is his claim. Hermes is his pick, not a tested comparison. Be careful what files and accounts you connect.

videos.title: Trump's 2027 Plan To Erase The $40T National Debt Crisis
videos.gist: The government won't pay off the $40T debt. It will try to outgrow it or inflate it away, so he says invest where that money goes.

points.title: The gap
points.text: About $5T in taxes in 2025 vs about $7T spent.

points.title: The Fed is losing money
points.text: It earns about 2% on old loans but pays banks about 4%.

points.title: Plan 1: borrow short
points.text: More short-term debt after long-term lenders pulled back.

points.title: Plan 2: stablecoins buy debt
points.text: From Jan 2027 they must be backed by dollars or Treasuries.

points.title: Plan 3: gold and Bitcoin
points.text: Gold is booked at $42/oz. Revaluing near $4,000 adds about $1T.

points.title: Plan 4: own stocks
points.text: Stakes in about two dozen companies, like Intel and MP Materials.

points.title: Midterm effect
points.text: Democrats winning Congress makes Trump's agenda harder to pass.

todo: His follow-the-money list: AI (AIQ), robotics (ROBO), chips (SMH), rare earths (REMX), defense (ITA), data centers (DTCR), quantum (QTUM)
Keep a cash cushion for a dip: high-yield savings at about 4%, or SGOV
Hedge against the dollar: gold (GLD), Bitcoin (IBIT), international stocks (VXUS)

stamps.label: Why the Fed is losing billions

videos.watch: His '$300,000 of Bitcoin' for the government sounds misspoken (widely reported in billions). Money Pickle sponsor and paid livestream pitch.

videos.title: How Cooked Are We? BTC Post Midterm Price + the Last Growth Engine
videos.gist: Midterm day after a brutal month. He thinks the Bitcoin bottom is in, and AI power is the last real growth engine.

points.title: Power is the bottleneck
points.text: Morgan Stanley: US data centers 70 GW short through 2028.

points.title: Fear is high
points.text: Crypto fear and greed at 26. Stocks at extreme fear.

points.title: ETF money leaving
points.text: Bitcoin ETFs red 4 of the last 5 weeks. Ethereum 7 of 8.

points.title: Support holding
points.text: Bitcoin near $77,500, on the short-term holder price ($77–78K).

points.title: Options lean bullish
points.text: Nearly 70% of open options are calls, with bets at $100K and $120K.

points.title: One growth engine
points.text: He says without AI data centers the US is in a severe recession.

points.title: Tesla FSD
points.text: Subscriptions up about 70% a year. A billion self-driving miles every 20 days.

todo: Watch whether Bitcoin holds the $77–78K support
Watch weekly Bitcoin ETF flows for a turn from red to green
videos.watch: Permabull with a Patreon and paid models. The 13 GW target, Anthropic valuation cut and SpaceX IPO ranking are his claims.

videos.title: Midterm Chaos (I LOVE It). Bitcoin's 13–71 Day Window
videos.gist: A calm, honest read: Bitcoin has bottomed weeks after the midterms, not on the day.

points.title: Bottom comes after
points.text: 71 days after in 2014, 39 in 2018, 13 in 2022.

points.title: Gap is shrinking
points.text: He guesses maybe a week this time.

points.title: Post-midterm S&P
points.text: Burry's data: +2% at 1 month, +10% at 3, +17.5% at 6, +15.5% at 1 year.

points.title: Binance hack handled
points.text: Binance covered $6.3B from its own balance sheet. Everyone got paid out.

points.title: Funds frozen
points.text: FBI, IRS, Tether and Circle froze about $2.5B.

points.title: Malware warning
points.text: Android TV boxes from one maker shipped with malware on 1.3M devices.

points.title: His picks
points.text: Solana, a little BNB, maybe Ethereum, Tron. Energy and nuclear next.

todo: Watch the weeks after the midterms, not election day itself
Treat the 13–71 day pattern as 3 data points, not a timing rule
videos.watch: Only 3 data points. He admits he sold in the bear market last time. Conference ticket link and iTrust Crypto IRA sponsor.

videos.title: Crypto Is About To Get INSANE… You've Been Warned!
videos.gist: Bitcoin sits on its 50-week average and the midterms may clear a worry. He calls today's fear a bear trap.

points.title: 50-week average
points.text: Bitcoin is at a level it bounced off in past bull markets.

points.title: RSI breakout
points.text: Weekly RSI broke a 2-year downtrend and is retesting it.

points.title: Wall of worry (Tom Lee)
points.text: Markets don't need good news, just one worry cleared.

points.title: Gridlock helps
points.text: Divided government means less new policy.

points.title: Big money moving in
points.text: Fidelity and Citi Wealth pitch spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs to clients.

points.title: Stick to top names
points.text: A token launches in 13 seconds, so most fail. Favors the top 20–50.

todo: Check Bitcoin against its 50-week average yourself
His view: stick to the top 20–50 coins, not new tokens
videos.watch: Coinbase sponsors the channel and every link is a signup bonus. Chart patterns are not evidence.

videos.title: A Dip Like This Only Comes Once a Decade
videos.gist: Memory stocks fell 20–50% from June highs, but demand never left. He sees the dip as a rare buy.

points.title: The canary: SK Hynix
points.text: Hit by a China scare and a helium squeeze, still made about $62B profit in a quarter.

points.title: Cutting board = HBM
points.text: Fastest, priciest memory. Still 20–25% short after new capacity, he says.

points.title: Countertop = DRAM
points.text: Demand grows a bit faster than supply. UBS sees balance around 2028.

points.title: Pantry = flash / SSDs
points.text: First layer to loosen, around the second half of 2027.

points.title: Warehouse = hard drives
points.text: No new factories. Morgan Stanley sees shortages every year through 2028.

points.title: His 3-year forecast
points.text: Seagate and WDC about $3,000 per $1,000. Even his bear case assumes the shortage holds.

points.title: Buying SK Hynix
points.text: The US ADR costs about 48% more than the Korean shares. He prefers an ETF.

rows.title: Seagate
rows.detail: Hard drives, pre-sold through 2028. His top pick.

rows.title: Micron
rows.detail: Only US maker of both HBM and DRAM.

rows.title: Sandisk
rows.detail: Pure flash, loosens first. 8-for-1 split Nov 20.

todo: His approach: buy in small pieces over time, not all at once
Before buying DRAM, check your broker's fee (Fidelity adds 5%, up to $100 a trade)
Don't hold both SOXX and SMH: they overlap about 69%
Next scary memory headline: check SK Hynix's results before acting
videos.watch: Paid Mayfair Gold segment ($21,666 disclosed). Buy-the-dip pitch from a Patreon seller.

videos.title: A Once In A 100 Year Investment Opportunity Just Started
videos.gist: The S&P looks calm, but most stocks are already in a bear market. He thinks three things lining up make this a rare setup.

points.title: Hidden bear market
points.text: He says about 60% of US stocks are down 20%+ from their highs.

points.title: AI and chips hit hardest
points.text: His figure: 9 in 10 down 20%+, 4 in 10 lost half.

points.title: Index = about 8 stocks
points.text: A few giant tech names carry the S&P, so an index fund is one big bet.

points.title: AI spending digest
points.text: Weak players wash out, like railways and the internet, then survivors win.

points.title: Midterms clear the fog
points.text: He cites S&P gains averaging 16% in the 12 months after midterms.

points.title: Money taps reopening
points.text: M2 growing fastest in about 4 years. The Fed is buying again.

points.title: Market isn't the economy
points.text: 2020: 15% unemployment, record highs. 2022: low unemployment, market fell 19%.

todo: Look at what your index fund actually holds
Judge a business on 3 questions: sales growing, profits growing, good return on what it owns
Follow where money is flowing instead of marrying one stock

stamps.label: 60% of stocks in a bear market

videos.watch: A funnel for his free training and paid Winston app. The percentages are his, not checked. 'Never once in 50 years' overstates the data.

videos.title: Get Unstuck and Get More Done: 9 Principles
videos.gist: Being stuck is a clarity problem, not laziness. Get clear, calm down, then take the next small step.

points.title: Clarity, not laziness
points.text: Not acting means you lost sight of what, how or why.

points.title: What game am I playing?
points.text: Tie each dull task to your bigger vision.

points.title: Find the fear
points.text: Ask: what am I afraid of that makes this hard?

points.title: Morning brain dump
points.text: 3 columns: negative belief, its opposite, evidence it's true.

points.title: The next 10 feet
points.text: Act on the clarity you have. Confidence comes after.

points.title: No escape hatch
points.text: Find a reason big enough that not acting isn't an option.

points.title: Recommit, don't beat yourself up
points.text: See what led to the slip, then recommit for 24 hours.

points.title: Calm before you push
points.text: Action from stress makes more stress. Shift your state first.

points.title: Journal by hand
points.text: 10–15 minutes: thank, ask for what you want, ask for others.

todo: Make a sheet with 3 columns
Column 1: every negative belief you woke up with
Column 2: the exact opposite, written as a new decision
Column 3: evidence the new decision is true (ask 3 times)
Do 2–4 beliefs a morning, for about 30 days
videos.watch: Built from 7 podcast episodes. 3 were the closest match to the YouTube titles.

videos.title: Sales Objection Replies (Nick Ayala Shorts)
videos.gist: Whoever is explaining is losing. Agree, ask one question, then stop talking.

points.title: “Too expensive” / lowball
points.text: Repeat their number slowly and go quiet. Then: “Help me understand how you got to that.”

points.title: Discount request
points.text: “I can work with you on price. Which part of the work should we take out?”

points.title: “Competitor is cheaper”
points.text: “They might be. Can I ask what's included in their number?”

points.title: “No budget right now”
points.text: “If budget wasn't an issue, would this be a yes?” Then wait.

points.title: “Send me a proposal”
points.text: “Before I write it, what needs to be in there for this to be a yes?”

points.title: “Run it by my partner”
points.text: “What do you think they'll ask you?” Then offer to join that call.

points.title: “We went with someone else”
points.text: “What did they do that I didn't?” and “Can I check back in 90 days?”

todo: Write the key lines down before sales calls
Rehearse them out loud
Run the role-plays in the Notion playbook
After each line, stop talking and let them answer
